moodys.citation_text: Moody's 2023-09-26 'Ascension Health Alliance: Update to credit analysis' references the Aa2 senior rating with stable outlook in effect prior to the Sept 2024 outlook revision. No Moody's rating action on Ascension Health Alliance is reported between the May 2017 Aa2 affirmation and the September 25, 2024 outlook revision to negative, indicating Aa2/Stable was in effect on 2022-12-31. Inferred from rating-action chronology rather than a primary press release dated 2022-12-31.

sp.citation_text: Per Healthcare Dive (Oct 10, 2023) describing S&P's October 2023 action: 'S&P Global Ratings affirmed its negative outlook for the health system last week.' The companion Becker's coverage ('Ascension could face downgrade amid persistent operating losses', Oct 4, 2023) frames this as the action where S&P moved to negative on AA+. The exact date S&P first revised outlook to negative is not pinned down; secondary sources suggest it was during calendar year 2023 in response to FY2023 losses, so on 2022-12-31 S&P was likely still AA+/Stable. PARTIALLY VERIFIED — exact outlook on 2022-12-31 not confirmed from a dated S&P press release.

fitch.citation_text: Healthcare Dive (Oct 10, 2023): 'Fitch Ratings on Sept. 26 [2023] lowered the outlook for St. Louis-based Ascension to negative from stable' — confirming the prior outlook was Stable. Becker's separately reported Fitch's pre-revision rating as AA+. Therefore Fitch was at AA+/Stable on 2022-12-31.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Affirmed AA+ Issuer Default Rating and long-term revenue bond ratings; outlook revised to Negative from Stable
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: FY2023 operating loss of approximately $3 billion; persistent operating pressures from labor and staffing. Fitch said it anticipated Ascension could 'once again generate a consistent operating margin of around 3% within the next several years.'
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: 'Fitch Ratings on Sept. 26 lowered the outlook for St. Louis-based Ascension to negative from stable while affirming its default rating and $6.6 billion of bonds at AA+.' (Healthcare Dive, Oct 10, 2023). Corroborated by Becker's Hospital Review ('Ascension outlook revised to negative').

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Affirmed AA+ long-term rating; outlook revised to Negative (companion action to Fitch's Sept 26 move)
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: S&P cited 'Ascension's weakening financial profile, including persistent operating losses and lighter liquidity and financial flexibility, which could lead to a lower rating without meaningful improvement in fiscal 2024.' Expected return to profitability in FY2025.
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: 'S&P Global Ratings also affirmed its negative outlook for the health system last week.' (Healthcare Dive, Oct 10, 2023). The Becker's article 'Ascension could face downgrade amid persistent operating losses' is dated Oct 4, 2023 covering this S&P action. PARTIALLY VERIFIED — exact S&P press release date (Oct 4, 2023) inferred from trade-press chronology, not from a primary S&P URL accessible without subscription. It is possible S&P had already been negative before this date and this was a re-affirmation.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Affirmed AA+ Issuer Default Rating and long-term revenue bond rating; outlook remained Negative
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Reflected $1.8 billion operating loss for FY ending June 30, 2024 (with $402M in one-time non-cash write-downs and substantial losses from May 2024 ransomware attack), partially offset by $1.2B operating improvement in core operations. Fitch considered the asset-sale and cyberattack losses one-time in nature.
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: 'St. Louis-based Ascension... had its issuer default rating and long-term revenue bond ratings affirmed at AA+ due to its strong operational profile, key leverage metrics and robust balance sheet, according to a Sept. 20 Fitch Ratings report.' Outlook remained negative per the same report.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Affirmed Aa2 senior rating; outlook revised to Negative from Stable
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Moody's cited the potential cash impact of the May 2024 cybersecurity incident, several years of declines in operating margins, and challenges improving operating cash flow margins to pre-pandemic levels without relying on positive one-time items.
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Becker's Hospital Review (Sept 26, 2024): 'Moody's lowers Ascension's outlook... Moody's said the negative outlook reflects Ascension's challenges in improving operating cash flow margins to pre-pandemic levels without relying on positive one-time items... and any potential cash impact related to a cybersecurity incident.' Corroborated by Modern Healthcare ('Ascension cyberattack prompts revised outlook from Moody's', Sept 26, 2024).

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Bond ratings lowered (AA+ to AA, per subsequent OS disclosures showing S&P at AA stable)
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Persistent operating losses, FY2024 cyberattack impact, $1.1B net loss. The action title from the primary S&P disclosure URL is 'Ascension Health Alliance, MO Bond Ratings Lowered To ...'
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Primary S&P disclosure page titled 'Ascension Health Alliance, MO Bond Ratings Lowered To ...' indexed in S&P Global Ratings disclosure system, dated October 7, 2024. The page body returns HTTP 403 to anonymous fetch, so the destination rating ('AA') and outlook ('Stable') are corroborated from the September 2025 Bond Buyer downgrade article ('Fitch downgrades Ascension Health to AA') which states 'The revenue bonds are rated Aa2 with a negative outlook by Moody's Ratings and AA with a stable outlook by S&P Global Ratings.' That language implies S&P had already lowered to AA prior to Sept 2025. PARTIALLY VERIFIED — title confirms a downgrade in Oct 2024; new rating inferred from later OS language rather than the press release body itself.

moodys.citation_text: Moody's Aa2/Negative as of Sept 25, 2024 was the last Moody's action before window end; per Bond Buyer Sept 2025 ('Fitch downgrades Ascension Health to AA'), 'The revenue bonds are rated Aa2 with a negative outlook by Moody's Ratings...' — confirming Aa2/Negative remained in effect through and past 2025-03-31.

sp.citation_text: Bond Buyer (Sept 2025): 'The revenue bonds are rated... AA with a stable outlook by S&P Global Ratings.' Combined with the Oct 7, 2024 S&P disclosure title 'Ascension Health Alliance, MO Bond Ratings Lowered To ...', S&P stood at AA/Stable on 2025-03-31. PARTIALLY VERIFIED — outlook ('Stable') for the post-downgrade S&P rating is sourced from the Sept 2025 OS-style language quoted in Bond Buyer, not from a dated S&P press release body.

fitch.citation_text: Fitch's Sept 20, 2024 annual review affirmed AA+ with Negative outlook; the next Fitch action was the Sept 17-18, 2025 downgrade to AA, which is AFTER the 2025-03-31 window end. Therefore Fitch stood at AA+/Negative on 2025-03-31.

outcome_class_rationale: One agency (S&P) downgraded one notch (AA+ to AA) during the window, on or around October 7, 2024. Moody's revised outlook to Negative (no rating change). Fitch revised outlook to Negative (no rating change). Net: one notch S&P downgrade plus two negative-outlook moves at the other agencies. This qualifies as DOWNGRADE (single-notch). Note: the S&P October 7, 2024 downgrade is the load-bearing fact; it is supported by a primary S&P disclosure URL (title shows 'Bond Ratings Lowered To ...') but the full text body could not be retrieved (HTTP 403 to anonymous fetch). The post-downgrade S&P rating of 'AA stable' is corroborated by Bond Buyer's Sept 2025 Fitch-downgrade article quoting the standard OS-style ratings disclosure. If a downstream consumer requires fully-quoted S&P press-release text, this outcome should be re-verified against the S&P Global Ratings subscription portal or the issuer's 2025 Official Statement (e.g., S&P Global URL /id/3470382 'Ascension Health Alliance, MO $3.83 Billion Bonds').
